q: In a 1–0 home win in December 2006, Phil Jagielka spent the last half-hour in goal after Paddy Kenny was injured. Which club were Sheffield United beating?
hint: Jagielka, an outfield player, kept the clean sheet and made a save from Robin van Persie to seal one of the Blades' best results of that Premier League season.

q: Sheffield United were promoted to the Premier League as Championship runners-up in 2018–19. Which club finished above them as champions?
hint: The champions took 94 points; the Blades finished on 89, six clear of Leeds United, and Aston Villa came up through the play-offs.

q: Sheffield United's first-choice goalkeeper during their ninth-place 2019–20 Premier League season was on loan from which club?
hint: Dean Henderson played 36 league games on loan as Chris Wilder's newly promoted side, tipped by most pundits for relegation, finished ninth.

q: Who was Sheffield United's top scorer in 2002–03, with 16 league goals?
hint: He was a central midfielder rather than a forward, and finished with 22 in all competitions in the season United reached two cup semi-finals and the play-off final.

q: Arsenal beat Sheffield United 1–0 in the 2003 FA Cup semi-final. At which ground was the tie played?
hint: Freddie Ljungberg scored in the 34th minute in front of 59,170 and David Seaman produced a famous late save; Arsenal went on to win the cup.

q: Which Sheffield United midfielder scored both goals in the 2–1 League Cup semi-final first-leg win over Liverpool in January 2003?
hint: The homegrown midfielder struck in the 76th and 82nd minutes at Bramall Lane, but Liverpool overturned the tie at Anfield.

q: Who scored the penalty for Wigan Athletic that relegated Sheffield United on the final day of the 2006–07 season?
hint: The defender had left Bramall Lane for Wigan that January; his first-half penalty, awarded for a Phil Jagielka handball, kept Wigan up on goal difference.

q: In June 2020, Sheffield United were denied a clear goal when goal-line technology failed to register that the ball had crossed the line. The 0–0 draw was away at which club?
hint: Hawk-Eye apologised unreservedly, saying its cameras were blocked by the goalkeeper, a defender and the post as Ørjan Nyland carried Oliver Norwood's free-kick over his own line.
